findings.requirement: Each merge into main tidies away what the landed records supersede
findings.what: (1) The statement and example 2 keep any file a current confirmed record still cites, and the intent's wont repeats it, yet example 1 deletes the sub-project specs and plans that confirmed, non-superseded FEAT-001, 002, 003, 004, 005, 006 and 008 cite in their descriptions ("Spec: docs/specs/sp1-grounding-loop.md", "lane CAPTURE of docs/plans/next-plan.md", "lanes ... of docs/plans/sp6-plan.md", and so on). Run as drafted, the v2 landing hits its own keep-if-cited rule and sends itself to the debug workflow. The draft neither says the landing rewrites those FEAT descriptions (and their "Sub-project N" titles) before the deletion nor carves the landing out of the rule. State it in the statement or add an example: the landing rewrites the FEAT descriptions to cite no removed document, then deletes. (A FEAT is a record the tidy job must not leave dangling; nothing in the dump supersedes the FEATs.)

findings.requirement: Old log entries are compacted into one archive segment per kind
findings.what: (1)/(4) The compaction rule can starve confirmed behaviour that reads history. SR-042 (confirmed, 3 tests; superseded by P9, which keeps its calibration) builds its labelled set from the owner's past decisions, including revoked and undone records as the 'no' examples, each with the judge's logged confidence, and EX-1 says fewer than 20 labelled read-backs means the kind does not pass. Those are exactly the entries about superseded, retired or changed records that the assumption archives, and the statement only says an on-demand question about history 'may' read a segment. No example says calibration, a judge job or verify reads through the segments, so after the v2 compaction the labelled set can silently shrink below 20 and settling cannot be switched on. Add an example (calibration sees the same labelled set before and after compaction) and say that every command, not only plumb explain, reads segments on demand.

findings.requirement: Old log entries are compacted into one archive segment per kind
findings.what: (4) 'Older than the records they served' is the heart of the requirement but is observable only through the assumptions: the statement and examples never define it. Example 1 says 'most about records version 2 superseded' (vague), and there is no example for the other two cases the assumption invents: an entry naming no record ('older than the previous landing') and test-run evidence superseded by a newer run. Prompt, approval and merge-evidence entries are not exercised at all, although approvals are the pre-intent to record trail P3 says is kept. Put the three archive conditions into the statement and give each a given/when/then.

findings.requirement: Each merge into main tidies away what the landed records supersede
findings.what: (4) Example 1's then-clause says the pruned-worktree archive is 'gone in the landing's tidy commit', but the archive (C:/coding/plumb-wt/_archive-2026-10-16-worktree-untracked/) is outside the repository, as the intent's own assumption says, so no commit can remove it and the folder's removal is not shown by the commit's file list that the proof promises. Split it: files removed in the tidy commit, and the outside folder removed by the job and named in the plumb line. Also, 'the landing names' and 'the plumb line names what was removed' leave open where the list lives and when the line appears (the job runs in the background after the merge, so the turn's plumb line may come before it finishes).

findings.requirement: Each merge into main tidies away what the landed records supersede
findings.what: (3) Examples 5 and 6 are not the tidy job. Example 6 (a branch that still edits a removed spec merges and 'the deletion stands') is a second behaviour, merge conflict handling: git raises a modify/delete conflict at the merge, before any background tidy job runs, and the draft names no mechanism that settles it or that tells the agent. Either carry it as its own requirement with the mechanism (and say who tells the agent) or drop it. Example 5 (plumb explain answers from the records alone) is vacuous: SR-033's explain resolves records only and never reads docs, so the removal changes nothing a reader can watch.
